# Requirements Document: How long a credential stays valid

## Introduction

A credential carries the instant its validity ends.  The guide says how an
issuer sets it for a boarding pass (§4.1.2, implementation consideration 1)
and says a verifier checks time validity (§4.2.1.2, step 6).  It gives no rule
for a photoid.  The guide puts revocation out of scope (§1.4), so within its
rules a credential from a trusted issuer stops being accepted only when its
validity ends.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneId/Validity.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Validity.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the sections of the guide each rule was written from, *External specifications* lists the specifications it relies on and whether this project has read each, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement OID-104

**User Story:** As an airline, I want a boarding pass credential to stop being valid shortly after the journey's last flight leaves, so that it cannot be presented again once the journey is over.

**Rule:** WHEN an issuer signs a boarding pass THE SYSTEM SHALL accept its validity only if it ends on or soon after the departure of the last leg of the journey. (Lean: `BoardingPass.validityFindings`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.2 Boarding pass](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §9.3.1, and the validity information set when an mdoc is signed (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF the validity of a boarding pass ends before the departure of the last leg of its journey THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-104.1, proven: proven theorem `validity_reaches_departure`
2. IF the validity of a boarding pass ends later than soon after the departure of the last leg of its journey THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-104.2, proven: proven theorem `validity_ends_soon_after`
3. WHILE the current time is before the departure of the last leg of the journey THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as not expired.
   - OID-104.3, proven: proven theorem `valid_before_departure`
4. WHEN the journey is completed THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as expired.
   - OID-104.4, open: open theorem `expired_once_journey_completed`; example `validAfterTheJourney`
5. WHILE the last leg of the journey has not actually departed THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as not expired.
   - OID-104.5, open: open theorem `valid_until_actual_departure`; example `expiredBeforeADelayedDeparture`; example `signedAgainAfterADelay`

#### Open question on OID-104.4

> An accepted boarding pass is expired once the journey is completed, for a
> journey that is completed no earlier than its last leg departs.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide says the end of validity MUST be
> "on or soon after last leg journey departure" and that this makes the
> boarding pass expire once the journey is completed.  It gives no limit for
> "soon after" and no definition of a completed journey.  If "soon after" is a
> day, a boarding pass for a two-hour flight is still valid twenty-two hours
> after landing, and since the guide puts revocation out of scope no rule of
> the guide ends it sooner.  The example `validAfterTheJourney` shows it.
> How long after the last departure may the validity of a boarding pass run?

#### Open question on OID-104.5

> An accepted boarding pass is not expired before its last leg actually
> departs.
>
> Open question for the business.  An issuer knows only the scheduled departure
> when it signs the boarding pass.  Under the reading that the scheduled
> departure is meant, the validity may end at any instant from that departure
> on, so a boarding pass can expire before a delayed flight boards, and the
> guide does not say whether the airline issues a new one.  The example
> `expiredBeforeADelayedDeparture` shows it.  If the airline signs the
> boarding pass again to end soon after the actual departure, that boarding pass
> is correctly issued under the reading that the actual departure is meant and
> wrongly issued under the other, and expiry, the time check a relying party
> makes, gives the same answer under both.  The example
> `signedAgainAfterADelay` shows it.  Which departure is meant, and
> what happens to a boarding pass credential when its flight is delayed past the
> end of its validity?

### Requirement OID-105

**User Story:** As a relying party, I want a credential to count as expired once its validity has ended, so that I never act on a boarding pass or a photoid that is no longer in force.

**Rule:** WHEN the current time is after the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as expired. (Lean: `expired`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.2 Boarding pass](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.2.1.2 Remote presentation using mdoc over the DC API](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §9.3.1, and the validity information set when an mdoc is signed (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the current time is after the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as expired.
   - OID-105.1, proven: proven theorem `expired_after_validUntil`
2. WHILE the current time is before the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as not expired.
   - OID-105.2, proven: proven theorem `valid_before_validUntil`
3. WHEN a credential has expired THE SYSTEM SHALL treat it as expired at every later time.
   - OID-105.3, proven: proven theorem `expired_stays_expired`
4. WHILE the current time is no later than the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as not expired.
   - OID-105.4, open: open theorem `valid_at_validUntil`; example `atTheEndOfValidity`

#### Open question on OID-105.4

> A credential is not expired at the exact instant its validity ends.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide says a verifier checks time
> validity and leaves the check to ISO/IEC 18013-5, which this project has not
> read.  If the validity ends at the instant itself, a boarding pass whose
> validity was set to end exactly at departure is refused at the moment of
> departure.  The example `atTheEndOfValidity` shows both readings.  Is a
> credential still valid at the exact instant its validity ends?

### Requirement OID-108

**User Story:** As a border authority, I want a photoid to stop being valid when the passport it was derived from expires, so that an expired passport is not accepted in digital form.

**Rule:** WHEN an issuer signs a photoid THE SYSTEM SHALL accept its validity only if it ends no later than the allowed limit for the document it was derived from. (Lean: `Photoid.validityFindings`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.1 photoid](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §1.4 Technical Guidance Scope](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [Readings of how long a photoid stays valid, where the guide states no rule](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Validity.lean) (modeller)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §9.3.1, and the validity information set when an mdoc is signed (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the document a photoid was derived from has expired THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the photoid as expired.
   - OID-108.1, open: open theorem `photoid_expires_with_document`; example `photoidOutlivesItsPassport`

#### Open question on OID-108.1

> A photoid whose validity was accepted is expired once the document it was
> derived from has expired.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide sets the validity of a boarding
> pass and says nothing about the validity of a photoid, and it puts revocation
> out of scope.  Under the reading that the issuer may set any end of validity,
> a photoid stays valid after its passport expires.  The example
> `photoidOutlivesItsPassport` shows it.  Must the validity of a photoid
> end no later than the expiry of the passport it was derived from?
